Возможно также сочетание сильного и слабого слогов (например, в пупео, в меньшей степени в лаха, при практическом отсутствии в гэлао). Структура сильного слога CVC или C1C2VC3. Сильный слог всегда тонирован, он ударный, занимает конечную позицию. Структура слабого слога CV, он всегда безударный и предшествует сильному; в пупео тонируется «нейтральным» ровным средним тоном, в лаха тон слабого слога повторяет этимологический тон сильного слога. ... В пупео пять тонов, в гэлао и лаха — шесть.

new_statements.translation: In the Kadai languages a simple word or morpheme is represented mainly by a strong syllable. A combination of a strong and a weak syllable is also possible (e.g. in Pupeo, to a lesser extent in Laha, and practically absent in Gelao). The structure of the strong syllable is CVC or C1C2VC3. The strong syllable is always tone-bearing, it is stressed, and it occupies the final position. The structure of the weak syllable is CV; it is always unstressed and precedes the strong one; in Pupeo it carries a 'neutral' level mid tone, in Laha the tone of the weak syllable repeats the etymological tone of the strong syllable.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Laha is a six-tone language whose native words are either a single strong syllable or weak+strong (sesquisyllabic/disyllabic); stress is fixed on the strong syllable, which is always word-final, while the preceding CV weak syllable is always unstressed (iambic pattern). In Laha the weak syllable copies the strong syllable's tone rather than taking a neutral tone.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the statement notes weak+strong words are less frequent in Laha than in Pupeo. (Ostapirat 2000 fn. adds that in Ta Mit Laha tone /343/ often becomes /24/ when preceded by another syllable, a sandhi fact, not an exception to stress placement.)
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (simple word/morpheme shape: weak syllable + final strong stressed syllable); statement is generic for the Kadai (Kra) group with Laha explicitly named; written by the fieldworker-author of the 1986 Laha grammar (Nong Lay / Khla Phlao variety, Son La). Tonal language with a stress statement.
new_statements.identity_note: The LES statement is framed for the Kadai (Kra) group as a whole with Laha named explicitly; Solntseva's own Laha fieldwork (1979 expedition) was on the southern Nong Lay / Khla Phlao variety of Thuận Châu, Sơn La (Glottolog 'Laha (Son La)'), not the northern Ta Mit (Lào Cai) variety described by Edmondson & Gregerson 1997. Both fall under laha1250.

sources.note: Family-level entry by the author of the 1986 Laha grammar: words are a strong syllable optionally preceded by a weak syllable (in Pupeo, less so in Laha); the strong syllable is always tone-bearing, stressed and word-final; the weak CV syllable is always unstressed and precedes it; in Laha the weak syllable's tone repeats the etymological tone of the strong syllable.
